question: Instituted in 1984, the National-level Lata Mangeshkar Award is given to promote excellence in the area of light music annually by the ________ government's culture department.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Lata Mangeshkar Award was instituted in 1984 by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, and is conferred annually by the state's Department of Culture for outstanding contribution to light music (sugam sangeet) and film music. (लता मंगेशकर पुरस्कार — मध्य प्रदेश सरकार, 1984)

• The award carries a cash prize along with a citation, and has been given to eminent musicians such as Naushad, Kishore Kumar, Jaidev, Manna Dey, Khayyam and Asha Bhosle.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Madhya Pradesh also instituted other national awards named after cultural icons — the Kalidas Samman, the Kishore Kumar Samman (for cinema), the Tansen Samman (for Hindustani classical music) and the Iqbal Samman (for Urdu literature).

• Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022), the "Nightingale of India", was born in Indore, Madhya Pradesh — which is why the state named the award after her. She received the Bharat Ratna (2001), the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989) and the Padma Vibhushan.

NOTE

• Do not confuse this with the Maharashtra government's Lata Mangeshkar Award or the Lata Deenanath Mangeshkar Award given by the Mangeshkar family trust in Mumbai.

question: The Sakraat festival is celebrated with the ‘Budigali’ or ‘Kalasi’ dance in ___________, where women take part in this dance, carrying decorative pots on their heads.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sakraat festival (the local form of Makar Sankranti) is celebrated in Odisha with the "Budigali" or "Kalasi" dance, in which women dance carrying decorated pots (kalash) on their heads. (ओडिशा — सकरात / बुड़िगली नृत्य)

• Balancing pots on the head while dancing is a hallmark of this harvest-season folk performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Odisha: Ghumura, Chhau (Mayurbhanj), Ranappa, Danda Nata, Dalkhai, Karma Naach and Sambalpuri. Its classical dance is Odissi.

• Famous festivals of Odisha: Rath Yatra (Puri), Raja Parba, Nuakhai, Konark Dance Festival and Bali Jatra.

NOTE

• Makar Sankranti is known by different names across India: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Magh Bihu (Assam), Lohri/Maghi (Punjab), Uttarayan (Gujarat), Khichdi (Uttar Pradesh) and Poush Sankranti (West Bengal).

question: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a welfare programme being administered by which Ministry of Government of India?
option_3: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Rural Development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a centrally sponsored social security scheme administered by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India. It was launched on 15 August 1995. (राष्ट्रीय सामाजिक सहायता कार्यक्रम — ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय)

• It gives effect to Article 41 of the Constitution (a Directive Principle) which directs the State to provide public assistance in cases of old age, sickness, disablement and unemployment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The NSAP consists of five components:

◦ Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)

◦ Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS)

◦ Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS)

◦ National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS)

◦ Annapurna Scheme (10 kg of free foodgrain per month to eligible elderly persons)

• Benefits are targeted at Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.

NOTE

• Other major schemes of the Ministry of Rural Development: MGNREGA, PMAY-Gramin, DAY-NRLM, DDU-GKY, PMGSY and the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission.

question: What is the main source of income for commercial banks?
option_4: Interest earned on loans and advances
solution_text:
The correct answer is Interest earned on loans and advances.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A commercial bank accepts deposits from the public at a lower rate of interest and lends that money as loans and advances at a higher rate. The difference between the two rates — the "spread" or net interest margin — is the bank's main source of income. (ऋण एवं अग्रिम पर अर्जित ब्याज)

• This interest income is far larger than the bank's non-interest income (fees, commission, lockers, remittances, etc.).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong — banks do not run on donations; they are commercial, profit-making institutions.

• Option 2 is wrong — banks have strict limits on stock market exposure under RBI regulations, so it is not their main income.

• Option 3 is wrong — government grants are given to development agencies, not to commercial banks as routine income.

• Bank functions: primary (accepting deposits, granting loans) and secondary (agency and general utility services).

NOTE

• Key banking terms: Repo rate (RBI lends to banks), Reverse repo rate (RBI borrows from banks), CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio), SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio), NPA (Non-Performing Asset), MCLR and Bank Rate.

question: The Taj Mahal was built by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Taj Mahal at Agra, on the bank of the Yamuna, was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum), who died in 1631. (ताजमहल — शाहजहाँ)

• Construction began in about 1632 and was completed in about 1653. The chief architect is generally identified as Ustad Ahmad Lahauri.

• It is built of white marble from Makrana (Rajasthan) and is famous for its pietra dura inlay work and perfect symmetry.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Taj Mahal was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 and is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World (2007).

• Other buildings of Shah Jahan: the Red Fort and Jama Masjid (Delhi), the Moti Masjid (Agra Fort), the Shalimar Bagh (Lahore) and the city of Shahjahanabad. His reign (1628–1658) is called the Golden Age of Mughal architecture.

NOTE

• Other Mughal monuments: Humayun's Tomb, Delhi (built by his widow Bega Begum — the first great Mughal garden tomb), Fatehpur Sikri and Buland Darwaza (Akbar), Itmad-ud-Daulah's Tomb, Agra (Nur Jahan, during Jahangir's reign) and the Bibi ka Maqbara, Aurangabad (Aurangzeb's era).

question: Who among the following made Ganesh Chaturthi popular as a public celebration in Maharashtra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak transformed Ganesh Chaturthi from a private household ritual into a large public festival (Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav) in Maharashtra in 1893. (लोकमान्य तिलक — सार्वजनिक गणेशोत्सव, 1893)

• His aim was to bring people of all castes together and to create a lawful public platform for nationalist mobilisation, since British rules restricted political gatherings but not religious ones.

• He also started the Shivaji Jayanti festival in 1895 for the same purpose.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tilak was called "Lokmanya" (accepted by the people) and was described by the British as "the Father of Indian Unrest".

• His famous slogan: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."

• He founded the newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English), and wrote Gita Rahasya while imprisoned in Mandalay.

• With Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal, he formed the extremist trio "Lal-Bal-Pal".

NOTE

• Tilak co-founded the All India Home Rule League (1916, Belgaum/Pune); Annie Besant started a parallel Home Rule League at Madras in 1916.

question: Which country’s Constitution was the inspiration behind the Directive Principles of the Indian Constitution?
option_2: The Constitution of the United States
option_3: The Constitution of the United Kingdom
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Constitution of Ireland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Indian Constitution, were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which had itself taken the idea from the Spanish Constitution. (नीति निदेशक तत्व — आयरलैंड)

• DPSPs are non-justiciable (not enforceable by any court) but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37).

• Dr B. R. Ambedkar called them a "novel feature" of the Constitution; they aim at establishing a welfare state and economic and social democracy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other borrowings from Ireland: the method of election of the President, and the nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha.

• From the USA: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, an independent judiciary, impeachment of the President, removal of Supreme Court/High Court judges, the post of Vice-President.

• From the UK: the parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, the writs, the cabinet system.

• From Australia: the Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce, joint sitting of the two Houses.

NOTE

• Key DPSP Articles: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code), Article 45 (early childhood care), Article 47 (nutrition and public health), Article 48A (protection of environment, added by the 42nd Amendment) and Article 51 (promotion of international peace).

question: When one stone is thrown upwards, what type of energy conversion would occur?
option_1: Kinetic energy would change to mechanical energy
option_2: Potential energy would change to gravitational energy
option_3: Mechanical energy would change to kinetic energy
option_4: Kinetic energy would change to gravitational potential energy
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kinetic energy would change to gravitational potential energy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a stone is thrown upwards, it starts with a large kinetic energy (KE = ½mv²). As it rises, its speed decreases and its height increases, so KE is steadily converted into gravitational potential energy (PE = mgh). (गतिज ऊर्जा → गुरुत्वीय स्थितिज ऊर्जा)

• At the highest point the velocity becomes zero, so the KE is zero and the PE is maximum.

• While falling back, the reverse happens — PE is converted back into KE. In the absence of air resistance the total mechanical energy (KE + PE) remains constant, illustrating the law of conservation of energy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong — mechanical energy is the sum of KE and PE, so KE cannot "change into" mechanical energy.

• Option 2 is wrong — "gravitational energy" is potential energy; there is no such conversion.

• Option 3 is wrong — mechanical energy is not a separate form that converts into kinetic energy.

• Formulae: KE = ½mv², PE = mgh, where g = 9.8 m/s².

NOTE

• The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.

• Everyday examples: a swinging pendulum (KE ⇄ PE), a hydroelectric dam (PE → KE → electrical), an electric bulb (electrical → light + heat).

question: Lack of functional small intestine can cause a malabsorption disorder leading to diarrhoea, malnutrition, weight loss etc. This particular condition is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is short bowel syndrome.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Short bowel syndrome (SBS)" is a malabsorption disorder caused by the absence or loss of function of a large part of the small intestine, usually after surgical removal or because of a birth defect. (शॉर्ट बाउल सिंड्रोम)

• Because the small intestine is where most nutrients, water and minerals are absorbed, its loss leads to chronic diarrhoea, dehydration, malnutrition, weight loss, fatigue and vitamin deficiencies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Down syndrome" is a genetic disorder caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21), leading to intellectual disability and characteristic facial features.

• Option 3 "Hypoglycaemia" means abnormally low blood sugar.

• Option 4 "Hyperglycaemia" means abnormally high blood sugar, typical of diabetes mellitus.

• The small intestine has three parts: duodenum, jejunum and ileum; it is about 6–7 metres long and its inner villi greatly increase the absorptive surface.

NOTE

• Digestion of carbohydrates begins in the mouth (salivary amylase), of proteins in the stomach (pepsin), and is completed in the small intestine by pancreatic and intestinal enzymes with the help of bile from the liver.

question: In December 2022, Government of India launched Grih Pravesh scheme. This scheme aims to provide benefits to the residents of ____ areas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is both rural and urban.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Grih Pravesh initiative of December 2022 was linked to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), under which completed houses were formally handed over to beneficiaries. Because PMAY runs in two streams — PMAY-Gramin and PMAY-Urban — the benefit reaches residents of both rural and urban areas. (ग्रामीण और शहरी दोनों)

• "Griha Pravesh" literally means the ceremonial entry into a new house.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• PMAY-Gramin was launched in 2016 (replacing the Indira Awaas Yojana) to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to rural households; it is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

• PMAY-Urban was launched on 25 June 2015 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, with the goal of "Housing for All". Its four verticals are In-situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR), Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) and Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC).

• PMAY houses are commonly registered in the name of a woman member of the household, promoting women's ownership of property.

NOTE

• Other flagship schemes launched in 2015: Digital India, Skill India, Atal Pension Yojana, Jan Suraksha schemes and AMRUT/Smart Cities Mission.

question: Indian Industrialists reacted against colonial policies that restricted business activities and formed an organisation in 1927. What was it called?
option_3: Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indian industrialists, reacting against colonial economic policies that restricted Indian business, formed the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) in 1927. (फिक्की — 1927)

• It was founded on the advice of Mahatma Gandhi by Ghanshyam Das Birla and Purushottamdas Thakurdas.

• FICCI is the oldest and largest apex business organisation in India; it supported the national movement and demanded protection for Indian industry, an indigenous currency policy and Indianisation of services.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) traces its origin to 1895 (as the Engineering and Iron Trades Association) but took its present name only in 1992; the year 1927 belongs to FICCI.

• Options 1 and 2 are fictitious organisations.

• In 1944, leading industrialists (J. R. D. Tata, G. D. Birla, Purushottamdas Thakurdas and others) prepared the "Bombay Plan" for India's post-independence economic development.

NOTE

• Related economic nationalism: Dadabhai Naoroji's "Drain of Wealth" theory (in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India), and the Swadeshi Movement (1905), which encouraged Indian-owned industries.

question: Who founded the All-India Forward Bloc Party?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The All India Forward Bloc was founded by Subhas Chandra Bose on 3 May 1939 at Makur, Unnao (Uttar Pradesh), after he resigned as President of the Indian National Congress. (ऑल इंडिया फॉरवर्ड ब्लॉक — सुभाष चंद्र बोस, 1939)

• He had won the Congress presidency at Tripuri (1939) by defeating Gandhi's nominee Pattabhi Sitaramayya, but resigned owing to differences with the Congress leadership.

• The Forward Bloc aimed to unite the radical, left-wing and anti-imperialist elements within the Congress.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Subhas Chandra Bose was called "Netaji". He reorganised the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) in 1943 and set up the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) at Singapore.

• His famous slogans: "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom", "Jai Hind" and "Dilli Chalo".

• Rasbehari Bose founded the Indian Independence League and formed the first INA in 1942, later handing it over to Subhas Chandra Bose.

NOTE

• Chandra Shekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh belonged to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA, 1928), not the Forward Bloc.

• Bose presided over the Congress sessions at Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939).

question: The Constitution allows __________ maximum members in Lok Sabha as of June 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 550.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 81 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550 — 530 members from the States and not more than 20 members from the Union Territories. (लोक सभा की अधिकतम संख्या — 550)

• The present actual strength is 543 (524 from States + 19 from Union Territories).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Earlier, Article 331 allowed the President to nominate up to 2 members of the Anglo-Indian community, making the maximum 552; this provision was discontinued by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 (with effect from 25 January 2020).

• The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of 250 — up to 238 representatives of States and UTs plus 12 nominated members (present strength 245).

• The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years; the quorum for a sitting of either House is one-tenth of its total membership (Article 100).

NOTE

• Minimum age: 25 years for the Lok Sabha and 30 years for the Rajya Sabha.

• The Lok Sabha is presided over by the Speaker; the Rajya Sabha by the Vice-President of India as ex-officio Chairman.

question: Which of the following novels is based on the partition of India and was written by Khushwant Singh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Train to Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Train to Pakistan" (1956) is the celebrated novel by Khushwant Singh set against the Partition of India in 1947. (ट्रेन टू पाकिस्तान — खुशवंत सिंह)

• It is set in the fictional border village of Mano Majra, where Sikhs and Muslims had lived peacefully until a train of massacred refugees arrives and communal violence erupts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "The Great Indian Novel" (1989) is by Shashi Tharoor — a satirical retelling of the Mahabharata as modern Indian political history.

• Option 2 "Untouchable" (1935) is by Mulk Raj Anand, on caste discrimination.

• Option 3 "Narcopolis" (2012) is by Jeet Thayil, shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize.

• Other works of Khushwant Singh: I Shall Not Hear the Nightingale, Delhi: A Novel, The Company of Women, Truth, Love and a Little Malice (autobiography) and A History of the Sikhs.

NOTE

• Khushwant Singh received the Padma Bhushan (1974) — which he returned in 1984 in protest against Operation Blue Star — and the Padma Vibhushan (2007). He edited The Illustrated Weekly of India and The Hindustan Times.

question: Which institution mainly provides financial assistance and support to microfinance institutions in India?
option_4: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SIDBI is the principal financial institution for the promotion, financing and development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in India, and it is the main body that provides financial assistance and capacity-building support to Microfinance Institutions (MFIs). (सिडबी — सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थाओं को सहायता)

• It was established on 2 April 1990 under an Act of Parliament, with its head office at Lucknow.

• Its SIDBI Foundation for Micro Credit (SFMC), launched in 1999, is the dedicated arm for channelling funds to MFIs for on-lending to poor borrowers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) is a department of the Ministry of Finance dealing with economic policy and the Union Budget — it does not lend to MFIs.

• The Ministry of Corporate Affairs administers the Companies Act and corporate governance.

• The Indian Banks' Association (IBA) is a voluntary association of banks, not a lending institution.

• SIDBI also runs schemes such as Udyami Mitra, PSB Loans in 59 Minutes and the Stand-Up India portal support, and it administers the CGTMSE credit guarantee scheme jointly with the Government.

NOTE

• Apex financial institutions in India: RBI (central bank), NABARD (agriculture and rural development), SIDBI (MSMEs), EXIM Bank (foreign trade), NHB (housing finance).

question: Mango showers are associated with which two states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala and Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mango showers" are pre-monsoon thunderstorm showers that occur in Kerala and coastal Karnataka during April and May. They are so called because they help in the early ripening of mangoes. (आम्र वर्षा — केरल और कर्नाटक)

• They also bring welcome relief from the intense summer heat before the arrival of the south-west monsoon in early June.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In Karnataka, the same pre-monsoon showers are also called "Blossom showers" or "Cherry blossoms" because they help the coffee flowers to bloom.

• Other local pre-monsoon storms:

◦ "Kalbaisakhi" or "Nor'westers" — violent evening thunderstorms in West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand and Assam.

◦ "Bardoichila" — the Assamese name for these storms.

◦ "Loo" — the hot, dry wind of the northern plains in May–June.

NOTE

• The south-west monsoon normally reaches Kerala around 1 June and withdraws from the country by mid-October; the north-east (retreating) monsoon brings rain to Tamil Nadu in October–December.

question: The Padma Shri awardee (2016) Gulabo Sapera is known as the Queen of ________ dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbeliya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gulabo Sapera, who received the Padma Shri in 2016, is world-famous as the "Queen of Kalbeliya dance". (गुलाबो सपेरा — कालबेलिया नृत्य)

• Kalbeliya is the folk dance of the Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan. The women wear flowing black ghagras (angrakhi) and perform swirling, snake-like movements to the music of the been (pungi) and the dholak.

• Kalbeliya songs and dances were inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan:

◦ "Chari" — performed with lighted lamps placed in a pot balanced on the head (Ajmer and Kishangarh).

◦ "Bhavai" — the dancer balances several earthen pots on her head while performing on the rim of a brass plate or on the edge of a sword.

◦ "Kacchi Ghodi" — a dance performed by men riding dummy horses, popular in the Shekhawati region.

◦ Others: Ghoomar (the state dance), Gair, Terah Taali, Kathputli and Chakri.

NOTE

• India's UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage entries include Kalbeliya folk songs and dances, Ramlila, Vedic chanting, Kutiyattam, Chhau dance, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja of Kolkata and Garba of Gujarat.

question: Who among the following is the author of the novel ‘Untouchable’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mulk Raj Anand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Untouchable" (1935) is the famous novel by Mulk Raj Anand. It depicts a single day in the life of Bakha, a young sweeper boy, and exposes the cruelty of untouchability and the caste system. (अनटचेबल — मुल्कराज आनंद)

• The book carries a preface by the English poet E. M. Forster and made Anand one of the pioneers of Indian writing in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other works of Mulk Raj Anand: Coolie, Two Leaves and a Bud, The Village, Across the Black Waters, The Sword and the Sickle and Private Life of an Indian Prince. He received the Padma Bhushan (1968) and the Sahitya Akademi Award (1971).

• Option 2 Salman Rushdie wrote Midnight's Children (Booker Prize, 1981), Shame, The Satanic Verses and The Moor's Last Sigh.

• Option 3 Vikram Seth wrote A Suitable Boy, The Golden Gate and An Equal Music.

• Option 4 Amitav Ghosh wrote The Shadow Lines, The Glass Palace, Sea of Poppies and The Hungry Tide; he was the first English-language writer to receive the Jnanpith Award (2018).

NOTE

• Mulk Raj Anand, R. K. Narayan and Raja Rao are together regarded as the "Big Three" founders of the Indian English novel.

question: Lachhu Maharaj is a celebrated ________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lachhu Maharaj (1907–1978) was a celebrated exponent of Kathak, belonging to the famous Lucknow gharana of Kathak. (कथक — लच्छू महाराज)

• He was a noted choreographer for Hindi cinema, having composed dances for films such as Mughal-e-Azam, Pakeezah and Mahal.

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), derived from the word "katha" (story) — the "kathakars" were storytellers who narrated epics through gesture and rhythm.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The three main gharanas of Kathak are Lucknow (emphasis on expression/bhava), Jaipur (emphasis on footwork/layakari) and Banaras.

• Other Kathak legends: Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Achhan Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Damayanti Joshi and Gopi Krishna.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India and their states: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: What is the name of the mascot for the 37th National Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Moga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The mascot of the 37th National Games, held in Goa from 26 October to 9 November 2023, was "Moga" — a stylised Indian bison (gaur), the state animal of Goa. (मोगा — 37वें राष्ट्रीय खेल का शुभंकर)

• The name "Moga" comes from the Konkani word "mog", meaning love and affection. The tagline of the Games was "Get Set Goa".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 37th National Games (2023) were inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium, Taleigao. Maharashtra topped the medal tally, followed by Services and Haryana.

• The 36th National Games (2022) were held in Gujarat, with the mascot "Savaj" (an Asiatic lion cub).

• The 38th National Games (2025) were held in Uttarakhand, with the mascot "Mauli" (a monal bird).

NOTE

• Some well-known Indian sports mascots: Shera (Commonwealth Games, Delhi 2010), Appu (Asian Games, Delhi 1982) and Olly (Hockey World Cup 2023, Odisha — an olive ridley turtle).

question: Ustad Allah Rakha and Ustad Zakir Hussain are both famous ________ players of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is tabla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Allah Rakha (1919–2000) and his son Ustad Zakir Hussain (1951–2024) were among the greatest tabla maestros of India. (तबला वादक)

• Both belonged to the Punjab gharana of tabla. Allah Rakha was famous for his accompaniment to Pandit Ravi Shankar's sitar recitals, which introduced Indian rhythm to Western audiences.

• The tabla is a pair of hand drums — the smaller wooden dayan (tabla) played by the right hand and the larger metal bayan (dagga) played by the left.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Zakir Hussain received the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2002), Padma Vibhushan (2023) and multiple Grammy Awards; he co-founded the fusion group "Shakti" with John McLaughlin.

• Instrument classification: tabla, mridangam, dholak, pakhawaj are percussion (avanaddha/membranophone) instruments.

• Option 1 veena — Chitti Babu, S. Balachander, Doraiswamy Iyengar.

• Option 2 bansuri (flute) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh.

• Option 4 sarangi — Pandit Ram Narayan, Ustad Sabri Khan.

NOTE

• Other famous instrumentalists: sitar — Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee; sarod — Ali Akbar Khan, Amjad Ali Khan; shehnai — Bismillah Khan; santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; mandolin — U. Srinivas.

question: Manika Batra won bronze medal in Asian Cup tournament. She is related to which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Table Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Manika Batra is an Indian table tennis player. In 2022 she won the bronze medal at the ITTF-ATTU Asian Cup in Bangkok, becoming the first Indian ever to win a medal at the Asian Cup. (मनिका बत्रा — टेबल टेनिस)

• At the 2018 Commonwealth Games (Gold Coast) she won two gold medals (women's singles and team event), a silver and a bronze — the most by any Indian at those Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manika Batra received the Arjuna Award in 2018 and the Khel Ratna (Major Dhyan Chand Award) in 2020.

• Table tennis is governed worldwide by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), founded in 1926 with headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland. In India it is governed by the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI).

• Other Indian table tennis players: Sharath Kamal, Sathiyan Gnanasekaran, Harmeet Desai, Sutirtha Mukherjee and Archana Kamath.

NOTE

• Table tennis terms: rally, service, let, smash, chop, loop, deuce, topspin, penholder grip, shakehand grip. A game is played to 11 points (win by 2).

question: What is the name of the geographic feature that serves as a boundary between India and Sri Lanka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palk Strait.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Palk Strait" is the narrow stretch of sea that separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal in the north-east with the Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar in the south-west. (पाक जलडमरूमध्य)

• It is named after Robert Palk, a Governor of Madras. The chain of shoals between Rameswaram (India) and Mannar (Sri Lanka) is called Adam's Bridge or Ram Setu.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 the "Strait of Gibraltar" separates Spain (Europe) from Morocco (Africa) and links the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea.

• Options 2 and 3 — the "Dardanelles" and the "Bosporus" straits lie in Turkey and, along with the Sea of Marmara, connect the Black Sea with the Aegean/Mediterranean Sea, separating Europe from Asia.

NOTE

• Other important straits: Strait of Hormuz (Persian Gulf–Gulf of Oman), Strait of Malacca (Indian Ocean–Pacific), Bering Strait (Asia–North America), Ten Degree Channel (Andaman–Nicobar) and Nine Degree Channel (Lakshadweep–Minicoy).

question: FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 final was held in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Navi Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 was played at the DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai, on 30 October 2022. (नवी मुंबई — फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022 फाइनल)

• Spain defeated Colombia 1–0 in the final to win the title. India hosted the tournament (its matches were held in Bhubaneswar, Margao and Navi Mumbai) and participated as the host nation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• This was the first FIFA women's tournament hosted by India. Earlier, India hosted the FIFA U-17 (men's) World Cup in 2017, whose final was played at the Salt Lake Stadium, Kolkata (England beat Spain 5–2).

• FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.

• The governing body of football in India is the All India Football Federation (AIFF), founded in 1937.

NOTE

• Major Indian football tournaments: the Durand Cup (Asia's oldest, since 1888), the Santosh Trophy, the Rovers Cup, the Federation Cup and the Indian Super League (ISL).

question: The Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO) was started in the year ________ at Sakchi in Jharkhand state.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1907.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO) was founded in 1907 by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata (the plant was set up under his son Dorabji Tata) at Sakchi, in present-day Jharkhand. (टिस्को — 1907, साकची)

• Sakchi was later renamed Jamshedpur in honour of Jamsetji Tata, and the railway station there is called Tatanagar. Steel production began in 1912.

• Sakchi was chosen because of its proximity to iron ore, coal and manganese deposits and to the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers for water.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jamshedpur is regarded as India's first planned industrial city.

• Other major Indian steel plants: IISCO Burnpur (West Bengal), Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Works, Bhadravati (Karnataka, 1923), and the public-sector plants of Rourkela (with German help), Bhilai (Soviet help), Durgapur (British help) and Bokaro (Soviet help), all set up under the Five Year Plans.

• TISCO was renamed Tata Steel in 2005.

NOTE

• The Hindustan Steel Limited was set up in 1954 and the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) in 1973 to manage public-sector steel plants.
